1. In respect of an accident, which is not in dispute and the liability of the insurer to pay the compensation is also not in dispute, the Tribunal has awarded the following compensation:

sentences.text: In arriving at the said compensation, the Tribunal has noticed that the claimant was a pensioner and as a result of the injuries, there was no question of any loss of future income.
In my view, the denial of the future income cannot be found fault with.

3. Having regard to the evidence on record, which indicates that the claimant had suffered 16% disability to the whole body, in my view, therefore, it would be just and appropriate to award a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards permanent disability.

4. Similarly, Rs.30,000/- awarded towards pain and suffering and Rs.20,000/-
awarded towards loss of amenities in life are required to be enhanced to Rs.50,000/-
and Rs.40,000/- respectively.
5.
A sum of Rs.78,800/- awarded towards medical expenses is affirmed, as the same is based on the documentary evidence.

6. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/-
towards food, nourishment, conveyance, attendant and other incidental expenses.

The evidence on record indicates that since the claimant had gone to Madras for treatment, it would be just and appropriate to award a sum of Rs.25,000/- towards food, nourishment, conveyance, attendant and other incidental expenses.

7. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the claimant would be entitled to the following compensation:
